gateway_review.classification: disclosed alternative, not a successful gateway receipt

metadata.review_scope: Updated assessment packet only; production code and implementation plan were not reviewed.

assessment_vs_plan_boundary: The updated assessment now identifies the scheduled-publication, full-platform lifecycle, and durable work-ahead authorization gaps. Analyze may choose the trigger policy, candidate/job schema, ownership lease, recovery algorithm, retry/cancellation behavior, supersession rules, and migration design; this review does not freeze those decisions. Residual findings are limited to unsupported evidence labels and one release-policy choice introduced too early.

findings.claim: Two current-state assertions still exceed the newly included evidence.
findings.evidence: research/current-state-evidence.json supports the project-wide 14/24 implementation count, active delivery-cadence-pipeline phase, five successful deliveries, no active iteration, and publicationDue=true. It does not provide a child-level registered-change count, a 2.2.9 release identifier, or an ownership/installed-acceptance record. Line 13 nevertheless says "this child has 0 registered implementation changes" and "The parent continues to own its 2.2.9 release and installed acceptance."
findings.suggested_fix: Add the child registry and parent release/acceptance evidence to the packet, or qualify those two statements as prior-handoff assertions and keep them out of design conclusions.

findings.claim: The assessment presents attempt counts as run receipts and attributes repeated-work causes that the supplied evidence does not contain.
findings.evidence: research/iteration-evidence.json exposes buildAttempts and runAttempts, not successful run receipts or per-attempt outcomes. Lines 17-23 label runAttempts as "Run checkpoint receipts." Line 27 further says checkpoint reasons describe ownership negotiation, runtime routing, rate limits, tool catalogs, provider budgets, and driver corrections, but neither supplied evidence JSON includes checkpoint reasons. The source audit supports only the narrower direct-build/repeated-for-Cadence-receipt example.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the table column to run attempts unless outcome-bearing receipt evidence is added. Limit causal claims to the one supported repeat-build case, or include the checkpoint-reason records and distinguish successful, failed, and administrative repetitions.

findings.claim: The assessment introduces incremental per-platform live-link publication before analyze has compared it with the current all-platform release completion contract.
findings.evidence: research/current-state-evidence.json defines completion as all four platform bytes published, metadata committed/pushed, landing deployed, and exact live URLs/bytes confirmed. Line 75 proposes that "As each verified platform artifact becomes available, a serialized publisher can update that platform's exact link while retaining previous valid artifacts for pending platforms." That can expose a mixed-version website and changes release presentation semantics; neither goals.md nor the assessed gap requires incremental public links. The assessment's own stage boundary says it does not freeze architecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Recast incremental per-platform publication as an analyze-stage option. Require analyze to compare atomic all-platform publication with candidate-bound incremental publication, including website consistency, rollback, and operator-visible semantics, before plan acceptance selects either policy.
